author: J.W. COOKE Keys
title: Coaching continuity providing stability across Keys athletics - NewsBreak
text:
By J.W. COOKE Keys ,
4 hours ago
In a place where coaching changes can happen as quickly as a job opportunity, a move or the challenges of living in the Florida Keys, athletic departments across Monroe County are entering the new season with something increasingly valuable — continuity.
Between Key West High, Marathon, Coral Shores and Basilica, just seven new varsity coaches were hired heading into the 2026-27 school year.
For four athletic departments separated by miles but connected by similar challenges, keeping coaches in place has become a major part of building successful programs. The reasons are familiar throughout the Keys: a high cost of living, extensive travel demands and many coaches balancing athletics with careers outside the school system.
The result is a collection of programs where relationships and culture have remained steady.
At Key West High, athletic director Andrew Freeman had only one opening to fill. Joe Henriquez takes over the boys and girls golf programs after Josh Bassett stepped away because of increased responsibilities at his full-time job.
Every other varsity coach returned.
Freeman stated the school looks for coaches who are already invested in the community and understand the responsibility that comes with working with student-athletes.
“We like to hire not just alumni, but people here that are in the community that have a good reputation and are good with the kids,” Freeman said.
That stability has allowed the Conchs to continue building a culture focused on more than competition. Freeman said 88 percent of Key West student-athletes last year either maintained or improved their GPA during their seasons, a number he credited to the work of coaches and teachers.
Marathon entered the offseason with two changes, both involving soccer. The Dolphins hired a new girls soccer coach and are still searching for a boys soccer coach, while Andrew Freeman returned to lead the volleyball program after stepping away from his previous role.
Athletic director Lance Martin explained the turnover in soccer has less to do with dissatisfaction and more to do with the realities of life in the Keys.
“It’s because they are not physically here, not because they didn’t want to keep coaching,” said Martin said.
The Dolphins also made a transition in track and field, with Helena Bursa moving into the head coaching role after Darby Sheehan became an assistant while accepting a position at an elementary school.
Martin said the evaluation of coaches goes well beyond the scoreboard.
“You can’t base anything on wins and losses this day and age,” said Martin. “You have to look at the overall picture. Is it running smoothly? Is it consistent with the kids, consistent with the parents? Are you giving the effort that is expected of you as a head coach?”
At Coral Shores, the Hurricanes experienced two coaching changes heading into the season, adding new leadership in boys tennis and wrestling while maintaining the rest of the athletic department.
For athletic director and football coach Ed Holly, maintaining consistency is critical as programs continue to develop.
The Hurricanes have focused on creating a culture where coaches are not simply teaching a sport, but helping shape the overall experience for student-athletes.
Like other programs throughout the county, Holly nited success is measured by more than wins and losses.
The goal is finding coaches who represent the values of the school and create an environment where athletes continue to grow.

The reasons are familiar throughout the Keys: a high cost of living, extensive travel demands and many coaches balancing athletics with careers outside the school system. Joe Henriquez takes over the boys and girls golf programs after Josh Bassett stepped away because of increased responsibilities at his full-time job.
